Guests at 11:15 AM: Dan Moos, Chief of Staff to Vice President for Administration and Finance Benson, and Karl Calvo - AVP Facilities.

AVP Calvo offered a slide presentation explaining how his office is structured into divisions dealing with long range planning and design, current operations, small projects, and large-scale construction.
Major projects planned include construction of additional undergraduate dorms, on-going improvements at the Bay Campus, and a new bio-medical sciences building, among others.
Of particular interest to FSEC were the future of the University Library and the need for additional graduate- and international-student housing.
Other issues the conversation touched upon included parking, lighting and other infrastructure improvements (like water treatment facilities and re-paving).
Google Maps layers of the university’s geographic information system were briefly discussed and it was noted that better mapping and better messaging about maps available would help address needs like understanding ease of access for members of the disabilities community and things like gender neutral restroom availability.
Classroom issues were also discussed, especially appropriateness of available spaces in relation to teaching style.

This process is complex and involves Dean-level requests for fit-outs of specific spaces, but also typically involves the JCSC, building managers, IT Services and CMS.
While the process may or may not have been well-coordinated in the past, AVP Calvo encouraged concerned faculty to reach out with specific concerts about their instructional spaces going forward.
Questions were asked about the wrap-up of the consultative process which led to the recently adopted Campus Master Plan, and whether all members of consultative committees had an opportunity to express their opinions of the draft plan.
Specifically, a final meeting of the committee was never convened and it is not clear whether originally planned broader ‘testing’ of the plan with campus groups as outlined by Sasaki happened.
It was conceded that given the outside consultants involved in the project, coordination may not have been as robust as it could have been and AVP Calvo offered to inquire about why the final meeting was not convened..
The conversation ended with a discussion of the library.
It was noted that faculty have grave concerns about the library’s current condition and its future.

AVP Calvo explained that the library’s location has been problematic from the start in that it was built over a stream and this has created ongoing issues with moisture in the building.
Several small projects are planned in the near term (HVAC, air handlers, roof - to deal with features/equipment that have reached the end of their useful life), but the university is also planning a $45 million renovation which will be a longer term project, perhaps in conjunction with the state archives. 1

4.
Priority Items 4.1 Relocating MPS to College of Education - see program - The program was created by the Graduate School and is offered through URI Online and is not located within any other degree granting college.
As the program is now ready to graduate its first class, a question arose about which college would host these graduates.
It was agreed administratively that for this December’s graduation event, the graduates could participate through the College of Education but a permanent solution is needed.
A proposal has been filed in Kuali to formalize the MPS in the College of Education.
FSEC members noted that the program involves Certificates from at least five colleges and many more departments so it is difficult to understand how the CoEdu was chosen over the other colleges involved.
The Executive Committee also had concerns related to the level of faculty control over this program, and how its revenue generation will be allocated.
For example, if housed wholly in Education, is the program a budget line therein, or does its revenue go to URI Online, or does it get divided among the other colleges that manage the certificates leading to this degree?

Could it lead to more faculty lines in Education?
FSEC members agreed much more information is needed beyond that provided in the Kuali submission and the Grad Council and other reviewers can be expected to have similar questions.
Pres.
Williams will correspond with the proposers to solicit more detail and to offer a heads-up that heavy scrutiny by faculty and the senate might be expected. 4.2 Green Hall Meeting Prep (10/29) - discuss agenda items - suggested so far: the Graduate School Report; the Diversity Council; IT/System Administrator permissions; ICE on campus and the need for a proactive policy; the Federal Compact; the rebranding of UCAS.
Pres.
Williams noted he and VP Preisser met with administrators yesterday and addressed some of these issues.
Other ideas for the joint conversation included a possible joint resolution on the Fannon Family gift, and the on-going effort to consolidate the 7- and 14-week calendars.
FSEC members should feel free to add topics to this possible agenda between now and 10/29. 4.3 Meeting Recap October 16 Senate meeting - see agenda - The meeting was generally efficient and productive.

The informational reports that were not delivered can be held until November.
FSEC agreed that other committee reports can wait until mid-year or as needed. i.
Status of four proposed Bills - The FSEC proposals are all expected to move forward, with some possible tweaks based on feedback from senators and review committees. ii.
FSEC role at senate meetings - FSEC agreed that in the interest of time, Executive Committee members should defer to other senators during discussion/debate at senate meetings except when explanatory comments about items being discussed are required for clarity. 4.4 Set weekly meeting schedule for spring semester - Starting in January, FSEC meetings will be held on Wednesdays from 11 - 1. 5.

Pres.
Williams will work with CTI Chair Wallace and liaison Daniels to address related IT issues referenced by submitters.
FS Leadership will ask for better information about gender neutral restroom availability to be made available to the community, and that they consider the need for additional such facilities.

Some faculty took umbrage at the request that they donate time “off the clock” to events like Homecoming and asked that the administration be reminded that work-life balance should be part of the community’s culture.
This led to a broader 2

discussion about faculty service generally and the fact that it is still not valued by the administration as it should be.
It was noted that some departments do a better job at fostering a culture of service than others and this often relates to some degree to the size of the department and the resources available. 5.2 Committee Assignment Updates - Finalize Joint Committees - Most assignments have been made but inquiries are still outstanding for a couple of seats.
FS Pres.
Williams will continue to follow up and staff will issue formal appointment letters. 5.3 Elimination of Budget Impact Statement Requirement - In drafting the change to UM 8.85.14, President Williams noted some related questions pertaining to the roles of SLOAA, JAPROA and College Business Officers that will need to be resolved before this amendment is discussed on the floor.

He will reach out to the ATL office and if answers are forthcoming, this legislation may still be introduced in November. 5.4 Might we also introduce legislation to either A) prevent students from repeating the same class more than twice (i.e., taking it more than three times) at URI; or B) require 'permission of instructor' for the second retake and beyond?
These issues were discussed through the lens of recent conversations around bills to modify the Second Grade Option UM language.
They are separate and distinct but related.
Introducing independent legislation dealing with the third (or more) attempt at a course seems advised.
There is a perception that “permission of instructor” is often the solution but there is still a coding burden that will fall upon Enrollment Services to carve out exceptions for dissertations, independent studies, etc.

Other issues will also need to be sorted (transfering in credit for a third attempt from another institution, for example) but FSEC will continue to discuss with the intention of advancing legislation later this year. 5.5 New library matters - Discussion ensued on a variety of challenges currently faced by the University Libraries. 5.6 Honors Program modification and HPR 403 Honors Reflections new course - Pres.
Williams briefed FSEC on the contents of two proposals recently put forward by the Honors Program. 6.
Updates 6.1 Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) i.
JCODL Updates - Meeting with relevant parties on 10/16/25 - The draft legislation was reviewed and is still being revised. ii.
Other - The FS Pres. and VP met with the University President, Provost and Vice Provost on 10/21.

Williams has set a meeting with Vice Provosts Adams and Bodah about the FS budget.
The FS Pres. and VP would like to propose a new approach to FS budgeting to ensure the type of service done by Officers, Committee Chairs, and Executive Committee members is adequately and fairly compensated.

They seek a new MOU to provide for payment to persons in those roles based on the model currently used for department chairs.
The current model that relies on “work release” in exchange for service is not working, in that such release is 2

at the discretion of deans and department heads and it is often not granted.
Negotiating a new MOU will also provide administrative clarity for staff to disperse funds, and will provide much-needed budgetary transparency for the faculty involved.

After formal adjournment, University President Marc Parlange, Provost Barbara Wolfe, and Vice Provost Sue Adams joined the meeting at 11:00 for their regular “once per semester” joint meeting with FSEC.
Meeting participants discussed items of shared interest and concern including the University Diversity Council, the creation of the Fannon Institute for Student Success and the reorganization of UCAS under the URI CARES rubric, the alignment of the standard 14-week calendar with the 7-week accelerated online calendar, and the potential for creation of a “President’s List” for high achieving students.

This led to a tangential conversation about advising generally and the move toward a professional advising model and how the faculty advisors in the departments fit in.
Some clarification regarding the university’s metrics on the availability of advisors seems warranted.
Regarding the calendar alignment initiative, the timeline for implementation was discussed, along with the level of effort required of enrollment services for the roll-out.
It was agreed that launching the concurrent enrollment option for graduate students only was a good idea.
Carve-outs for the ABM’s and a few other programs would need to be created, however.
